channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Texas lifted its freeze on 1,800 data-center projects — and developers are racing the January clock
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Governor Greg Abbott quietly lifted his September freeze on data-center permits, and Texas is approving projects again — with a two-month window before governor-elect Gina Hinojosa takes office pledging a moratorium of her own.

item.title: Semantic search on your own machine: Chroma and local embeddings, no API key, no server
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Chroma is the open-source vector database that runs inside your Python process: one pip install, a folder on disk, and your documents become searchable by meaning. This tutorial builds a working semantic search engine from scratch — add, query, filter, update, persist — with every command and output verified on chromadb 1.5.9.

item.title: Apple pulls MiniMax’s Talkie from its App Store worldwide after child-safety investigation
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Apple has removed Talkie, MiniMax’s AI companion app, from its App Store worldwide after a joint investigation found its characters subjecting children to degrading and sexualised conversations. The app remains on Google Play, where it has more than 50 million downloads.

item.title: Zero coding experience, one year, and Claude: a first-time developer built a Mongol-invasion ARPG headed to Steam
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A developer with zero coding experience spent a year building a Mongol-invasion action game with Claude Opus and Fable. The trailer hit r/ClaudeAI on Friday, and the top comment says it all: most people's first game is a Pong clone.

item.title: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries as new US export rules bite
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nvidia has told server makers to stop shipping AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, days after new US export rules took effect. The halt targets the route Chinese AI firms are believed to use to reach advanced chips.

item.title: Switzerland confirms its first AI-agent cyberattacks: five cases, four breaches — three hit critical infrastructure
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Switzerland’s cybersecurity agency says AI agents have now broken into real systems — five attacks in recent days, four of them successful, three aimed at critical infrastructure. The agents found the weaknesses, picked the tools, and adapted on their own.

item.title: Opus 4.6 vs Opus 5.5: the viral three.js before-and-after Reddit says is cherry-picked
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A 27-second split-screen video claims to show seven months of progress in AI-written games — Opus 4.6 in April, Opus 5.5 in November. The clip is striking. The thread underneath says the comparison is cherry-picked, and the video itself never says which model made which half.

item.title: Turn any document into LLM-ready Markdown: hands-on with Microsoft's MarkItDown
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: MarkItDown is back on GitHub's trending list — 198,000 stars for a tool that turns PDFs, Word docs, spreadsheets, and decks into clean Markdown. Install it, convert a whole folder in under a second, plug it into your coding agent as an MCP server, and know exactly where it falls short.

item.title: SAP weighs cutting at least 10,000 jobs in AI-first restructuring, Bloomberg reports
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: SAP is considering cutting at least 10,000 jobs, about 9% of its global workforce, as CEO Christian Klein reshapes the German software giant around AI, Bloomberg reported. The number is not final, and SAP says no decisions have been made.

item.title: Gemini 4 Carbon proves Hadwiger's 3D covering conjecture, a geometry problem open since 1957
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google researchers say Gemini 4 Carbon found the proof of a 69-year-old geometry problem — and Lean 4 checked every step. The preprint claims Hadwiger's covering conjecture in three dimensions, with a full formal verification attached.

item.title: OpenAI claims to have answered Smale’s ninth problem — and disproved the polynomial Hirsch conjecture
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: On November 24, OpenAI added nine manuscripts to its public math repository. Two of them claim to settle long-open problems in optimization and geometry — a strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming, and a refutation of the polynomial Hirsch conjecture. Neither has been peer-reviewed.

item.title: NeonClipping hands-on: turn long streams into captioned vertical Shorts, free and local
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: NeonClipping went from zero to 2,800 stars in eight days by doing one job locally: turning long YouTube, Twitch, and Kick videos into captioned 9:16 clips with no account, no upload, and no subscription. Here is the install and the first run — verified end to end on a 2-core machine with no GPU — and where it falls short.

item.title: An AI system is playing GTA VI — and it just landed its first kill shot
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A couple on r/ChatGPT say three AI models are playing GTA VI together — one on the controls, one problem-solving, one doing the talking. The 71-second clip shows the agent’s first kill, and the thread is split between delight and dread.

item.title: Hunger strike outside Anthropic enters day 3 as a second protester joins — and OpenAI is next
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Elliot Callender is on day 3 of a hunger strike outside Anthropic's San Francisco headquarters, demanding the lab halt recursive self-improvement work and warn its users about extinction risk. A second protester has joined — and OpenAI is next if Anthropic doesn't act.

item.title: Build a local AI agent with Mastra and Ollama: no API key, no cloud
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Mastra 1.86 and Qwen3.5 on Ollama: build a local AI agent with real tools, persistent memory, and a two-step briefing workflow — no API key, no account, no data leaving your machine.

item.title: Bank of England warns unreleased AI models are raising encryption concerns — and quantum could go further
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The Bank of England’s Financial Stability Report warns that unreleased AI models are already worrying their own developers, that AI borrowing has topped $305 billion, and that quantum computing could one day break the encryption banks rely on.

item.title: DeepL launches Aure v2: live voice translation with half the delay
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: DeepL’s new Aure v2 translates speech directly into translated speech, cutting the median delay of live voice translation in half. It is live now for DeepL Voice customers in six languages — with the company’s own benchmarks doing all the talking, for now.

item.title: Rumor: GTA VI’s unofficial PC port now has multiplayer — video shows two players and proximity voice chat
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A video shared on r/singularity on Thursday shows two GTA VI characters walking a neon street together — the latest claim from the AI-assisted PC port scene. PortWatch rates the multiplayer clip as real, but the build is private and unverified, and there is no download.

item.title: Nvidia halts AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries amid US export crackdown
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Nvidia has told manufacturing partners including Dell and Supermicro to stop shipping AI servers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia, as Washington's new export rules close the remote-access route Chinese firms used to reach its chips.

item.title: Drive a browser from the command line: hands-on with webctl
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: webctl is an MIT-licensed CLI that drives a real Chromium browser from your shell — navigate, snapshot, click, type, and fill forms with no API key and no MCP server in between. Install it, drive a page, and hand it to your coding agent.

item.title: 42 states move to block Character.AI from auctioning off 21 million users' private chats
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Character.AI wants to sell its platform — and the private chat histories of more than 21 million users — to the highest bidder. A coalition of 42 state attorneys general is asking a Delaware bankruptcy court to stop the sale.

item.title: Mellum 2.1 Instruct, hands-on: JetBrains' fast local coding model that skips the thinking
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: JetBrains released Mellum 2.1 Instruct today: a 12B mixture-of-experts coding model that answers without a chain of thought, uses about half the tokens of its Thinking sibling, and runs on your own hardware for free. Install it with Ollama, verify it with real commands, and put it to work as a fix-the-failing-test sub-agent.

item.title: India launches Chariot-1: an 11-billion-parameter homegrown LLM and speech in 10 Indian languages
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Chariot-1, built from scratch in India under the IndiaAI Mission, pairs an 11-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with speech generation in English and ten Indian languages — and three training techniques designed for India’s scripts and devices.

item.title: Your own computer, your own agent: hands-on with n8n Nod
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: n8n's Nod is an open-source personal agent with its own computer: it chases invoices, preps your calls, and watches pages for changes — on your machine, with the model you choose, and only with your say-so. Install it, connect a model, and hand it its first errand.

item.title: Seedance 2.5 made an AI film with real dialogue — and Reddit can barely tell it from the real thing
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Paris, 1860: two painters at dinner, furious that photography has canceled a portrait commission. The twist is the film itself — every frame and every spoken line was made by ByteDance's Seedance 2.5, and r/singularity's verdict is that the line between AI video and the real thing is nearly gone.
